call_points.text: No numeric FY27 guidance given; management expects sugar prices to stay firm on ~4.6 MMT closing stocks.
Key machinery installed and commissioned at the new Defence manufacturing facility; capex programme proceeding satisfactorily.
PTB product enquiries in Q4FY26 up 183% YoY; overall FY26 enquiries doubled over FY25.
Distillery tied up 17.18 crore litres of ethanol under OMC Cycle-1 and with private OMCs; expects further allocation.
PTB held PBIT margin at ~35% despite incremental capacity costs and lower revenue.
Management flagged urgent need to address ethanol overcapacity; sugarcane-based ethanol prices unchanged for three years.
West Asia conflict deferred PTB deliveries to global and domestic customers in Q4FY26.

operating_notes.text: NCLT Allahabad Bench pronounced the order sanctioning the Composite Scheme of Arrangement involving Triveni Engineering, Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises, and Triveni Power Transmission.

ICRA rates ₹3,110.37 Cr of Triveni Engineering bank facilities (₹326.93 Cr term loan, ₹1,825 Cr long-term working capital, ₹958.44 Cr short-term non-fund based) plus ₹300 Cr commercial paper carved out of working capital limits.
Sugar inventory as on 31 March 2026 was 59.7 lakh quintals valued at ₹38.1/kg, against 60.4 lakh quintals at ₹37.6/kg a year earlier.
Distillery FY26 sales were 213,453 KL at an average realisation of ₹61.0/litre, with ethanol 92% of alcohol sales and 56% of ethanol grain-based.
PTB closing order book ₹485 Cr at 31 March 2026, up 25%, with FY26 order booking ₹467 Cr and PBIT margin ~35%.
A penalty of ₹0.23 crore was imposed on the Shamli Sugar Unit by the CGST Division.

timeline.summary: Triveni Engineering announced that the NCLT Allahabad Bench pronounced the order on May 7, 2026, sanctioning the Composite Scheme of Arrangement.
Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd. postponed Q4 & FY26 Results Conference Call from May 18, 2026, due to delayed Board meeting, signed by Geeta Bhalla, Group Vice President.
On May 19, 2026, Triveni Engineering announced the effectiveness of the Composite Scheme of Arrangement following NCLT sanction.

On May 28, 2026, ICRA reaffirmed Triveni Engineering's long-term ratings at [ICRA]AA+ (removed from watch with developing implications, Stable outlook assigned) and short-term and commercial paper ratings at [ICRA]A1+, covering ₹3,110.37 Cr of bank facilities and ₹300 Cr of commercial paper.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,833.65 Cr (-4.8% YoY), net profit ₹167.45 Cr (-10.5% YoY).
Triveni Engineering's Q4 & FY26 investors' brief reported FY26 net revenue of ₹6,291 Cr (+10.6%) and PAT of ₹268.7 Cr; with the PTB demerging into Triveni Power Transmission from 1 April 2026.
Triveni Engineering announced board restructuring and committee formations for TPTL ahead of its proposed listing.
GEETA BHALLA, Group Vice President & Corporate Office, shared the audio recording of the Analysts/Investors Conference Call on Q4 & FY26 results via the company website on June 4, 2026.
Triveni Engineering received a tax penalty order of ₹0.23 crore for its Shamli Sugar Unit from the CGST Division.
